main_text.p: facturum. Sic Terent. Pollicitus sum facturum.
main_text.head: Cap. 22. De gerundio.
main_text.p: Gerundium regit casum sui verbi, Socr. φαῦλων ἔργων ἡ ὃς λόγους τοῦ ξαιπ-τέον, facinorum malorum sermones quoq; repudiandum. Plat. ψυχὴν αἰσχ-ρῶν, αἰσχρὰν ἡ ἀμέλησον ζητέον, animum a-mentem turpem & immoderatum statuendum: id est, animus amens pro turpi & immoderato habendus. ἐπεὶ τὸ μέσον τυγχάνει ἀκρως χαλεπόν, καὶ τὸν δεύ-τερον (φασὶ) πλὴν τῶ ἐλάχιστα λαμβάνειν τῶν κακῶν, cúm medium consequi summé sit difficile, secunda (ut inquiunt) navigatione, minima capiendum malorū. Quod Latini rariūs imitati: Plaut. Aliqua consilia reperiendum. Potiūs autem & sæpiūs dicitur per gerundiva, Consilia reperienda.

page.notes: Greek passages are printed with heavy diacritics and some letters are doubtful; rendered as best read. The final "Ali-" is a catchword-like hyphenated word at the foot right, kept as a paragraph. Page is a single text column; no margin notes visible.
